title: SEO and search data
for: keyword volumes and difficulty, rankings, SERP features, backlinks, site audits, Search Console performance

manual.export: Export the keyword, ranking or backlink report as CSV from the tool (Search Console: Performance > Export; Ahrefs and Semrush: the Export button on any report) and drop the file into the snapshots folder; data/seo/keywords.csv stays the canonical table.

vendors.name: DataForSEO
caveats: Wired in .mcp.json and .cursor/mcp.json today; the version is pinned at 3.1.1 and bumped on purpose in a proposal

The npx variant needs Node.js on the machine; the remote endpoint https://mcp.dataforseo.com/v3/mcp takes HTTP Basic auth (login:password base64-encoded), which .mcp.json cannot express as a ${VAR} header, so swap to it by hand and keep the credentials out of the file
Every call costs API credits; DATAFORSEO_USERNAME duplicates DATAFORSEO_LOGIN because different package versions read different names
Not in the Claude connectors directory

script.notes: the scheduled refresh: search volume and difficulty for every row of data/seo/keywords.csv into data/seo/snapshots/YYYY-MM-DD-dataforseo-volume.csv; --update also refreshes the canonical table

vendors.name: Ahrefs
caveats: Remote server only; the local ahrefs/ahrefs-mcp-server repo was archived in February 2026 and now points at the remote endpoint
OAuth on first use mints an MCP-scoped API key; Enterprise plans can pass an existing API key instead (header format not verified, so no key variant here)
Around 95 tools; each call consumes API units, paid plans Lite and above
Listed in the Claude connectors directory

auth.where: browser grant on first use; Ahrefs issues an MCP-scoped API key behind it

script.notes: copy scripts/seo_snapshot.py; an API key (Account settings > API keys) calls /v3/site-explorer/organic-keywords for a scheduled rankings snapshot

vendors.name: Semrush
caveats: Read-only by design; HTTP only (no stdio)
API units are billed per call; the Trends API needs its own subscription
The key variant uses the documented header Authorization: Apikey <key>
Listed in the Claude connectors directory

auth.where: Semrush: Subscription info > API units > API key

script.notes: copy scripts/seo_snapshot.py; the same key calls the Analytics API v3 (domain_organic report) for a scheduled snapshot

vendors.name: Moz
caveats: No official Moz server; the community metehan777/moz-mcp (15 stars, stale) says itself it is not official and is not on a package registry with a version to pin, so no stdio entry
Use the manual export, the Moz Links API in a script, or DataForSEO's backlink and rank metrics instead

script.notes: copy scripts/seo_snapshot.py; the Moz API v2 token (Moz Pro > API) calls /jsonrpc data.site.metrics.fetch for a scheduled authority snapshot

vendors.name: Google Search Console
caveats: community server maintained by AminForou (mcp-gsc, PyPI mcp-search-console, 1,485 stars, pushed 2026-07-29); judge as a script, not a vendor tool
write tool names not verified; deny the whole server (`mcp__gsc`) until checked (the writes are sitemap submission and URL inspection requests, not data changes)
Google ships no official Search Console MCP server as of August 2026

Auth is a Google service account JSON (add its email as a user on the property) at GSC_CREDENTIALS_PATH, or an OAuth client secrets file at GSC_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRETS_FILE for a browser login; the file path is not a secret, the file is
Alternative community server ahonn/mcp-server-gsc (npm mcp-server-gsc@0.3.0, Node) if Python is unavailable

auth.where: Google Cloud console: a service account with the Search Console API enabled, its JSON key on disk, added as a user in Search Console > Settings > Users

script.notes: copy scripts/seo_snapshot.py; the same service account posts to searchconsole.googleapis.com/webmasters/v3/sites/{site}/searchAnalytics/query for the weekly query and page snapshot; the Search Console API is simple enough that the script is the better unattended route

vendors.name: Similarweb
caveats: API-only, Business and Enterprise plans; every call consumes credits
The header name api-key comes from the Similarweb API reference security scheme; confirm on the MCP page when wiring
Listed in the Claude connectors directory

script.notes: copy scripts/seo_snapshot.py; the same key calls /v1/website/{domain}/total-traffic-and-engagement/visits for a scheduled competitor-traffic snapshot

vendors.name: Screaming Frog SEO Spider
caveats: The MCP server is built into SEO Spider v24 and runs from the desktop app on the licensed machine; the app shows its local endpoint and the connection snippet, which differ per install, so no committed entry
Not every feature is exposed; crawls are heavy and never run on a schedule from this repo
Community headless server bzsasson/screaming-frog-mcp (82 stars) wraps the CLI crawler; judge it as a script

cli.notes: screamingfrogseospider --crawl <url> --headless --export-tabs "Internal:All" --output-folder <dir> writes CSVs that copy into the snapshots folder

vendors.name: Bing Webmaster Tools
caveats: No official server; community servers (isiahw1/mcp-server-bing-webmaster and others) exist but were not verified to a pinnable package version, so no stdio entry
write tool names not verified; if a community server is wired, deny it whole until checked (its writes are URL submissions)
The Webmaster API with an API key is simple enough for a script

script.notes: copy scripts/seo_snapshot.py; the API key (Webmaster Tools > Settings > API access) calls ssl.bing.com/webmaster/api.svc/json/GetQueryStats for a scheduled snapshot
